guide: Open Start and type your center name, your own claim rates, the months between drills and the days between checks in the yellow cells. They are your own plan, check your local rules for what you must hold.
Check Rooms and Children. They hold the rooms and the children the other sheets look up; keep statuses and dates only, never health detail.
Fill the Menu with your menu cycle: one row per weekday and meal with the dish, the cost per child and the portions a kilogram.
Write the meal counts on Meals: children present, meals served and eligible meals by day, meal and room. Any meal served to more children than were present is flagged.
Read Menu Cost by Week and Food Purchases to see the food cost per child-day against your own average, and Meal Claim by Month before you send a claim.

Keep Health Records up to date: status (on file, due, missing), due date and last checked, one row per child and record. Status Board by Room, the Cook's Daily List and Missing Records Follow-up fill in.
Log every incident on Incidents: date, time, child, room, type, whether the family was told and whether the follow-up is done. Incidents by Hour and by Room and Month show the patterns.
Write each drill on Drills and read Drill Schedule by Month for what is due, done and overdue.
Log room checks on Checks. Check Completion by Week and Cleaning and Safety Schedule show completion by room and what is due next.
Use the 18 calculators for the menu, the claim, the status board, incident patterns, drills, checks, shopping, food cost and price rises.
Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in.
Read the Meals, Health and Safety Dashboard and Charts every week: meals, food cost, records, incidents, drills and checks.

listing.title: Childcare Center Meals, Health and Safety Excel Template: Meal Claim, Menu Cost, Records Status, Incident Log, Drills, Checks
listing.headline: Keep meals, records, incidents, drills and checks under control
listing.description:
Run the kitchen and the safety paperwork of a home daycare or childcare center in one Excel workbook. Built for an owner-director with 1 to 5 rooms. Meals go on one sheet by day, meal and room, and any meal served to more children than were present is flagged before you send a meal-program claim, a claim for meals served made to a food program. The menu cycle gives the cost per child, the kilograms for your order and the dearest dishes; Menu Cost by Week and Food Purchases show the food cost per child-day against your own last 12 months.

Health Records keep the status of each record (on file, due, missing) and its due date, never health detail. The Status Board by Room, the Cook's Daily List and Missing Records Follow-up show who needs an update and who to call first. Incidents record date, room, type, whether the family was told and whether the follow-up is done; Incidents by Hour and by Room and Month find the hour that repeats and compare a room with its own usual rate. Drills, the monthly drill schedule, Checks, completion by week and the cleaning and safety schedule help you keep track of what is due and what was missed.

18 calculators cover the menu and cost, the claim, the status board, incident patterns, drills, completion, shopping, food cost per child-day, over-orders, price rises and the diet list. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to families, the cook, the supplier, teachers and the cleaner. Children's data is names, rooms, dates and status only.

This is part six of the Home Daycare and Childcare Center suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, with a demo copy full of sample data to explore first. It helps you keep track of meals, records and safety paperwork; it does not promise results or replace your local rules.
